prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system spans River Intake Pump Station (Ironwood)/Raw Water Screen Channel–High Service Pump Header; excludes distribution.

Intake obeys withdrawal/demand/depth limits and start permissives; lost permissives alarm/stop. Screen sends Rake Torque Snapshot after cleaning; rapid changes require verification. Chief Operator authorizes Storm Intake Mode, targets, responses, stable-duration return, urgent dosing, sampling priorities; reviews deviations/recovery. Maintenance Planner schedules poststorm work.

Coagulant Dosing Skid (Marigold) meters coagulant, sends Alum Batch Ticket; Laboratory Technician verifies lot identity. Dosing requires verified feedback; loss invokes verified safe/fixed dosing plus grabs. Duty Engineer authorizes temporary turbidity adjustments/configuration changes; reviews consequential field/laboratory differences.

North Filter Gallery (Cobalt) records turbidity/headloss each scan; South Filter Gallery sends Filter Run Exception Note. Runs consider duration/headloss/turbidity/backwash/upstream conditions; postwash return requires rinse-to-waste targets/stability. Manual overrides require justification, monitoring, prompt restoration.

Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (Sparrow) receives custody-controlled samples; sends identifier/date/time-checked Jar Test Photograph Set. Laboratory Technician sends complete, legible Sample Chain Slip; checks labeling/container/holding-time/temperature/preservative/seals, records mismatches before acceptance, preserves custody/acceptance records for Chief Operator/Duty Engineer/regulatory auditors. Late/warm samples: troubleshooting only, not compliance. Review calibration/blanks/duplicates/standards before release; failed checks require investigation/documented correction or rejection. Verify mixing/settling/range for turbidity/particles; reagents/contact-time/timing for residuals. Field readings remain provisional pending location/time-matched laboratory comparison. Reconcile accepted results with collection time/point/process state/manual observations; notify Chief Operator of unsupported adjustments.

Chlorine Contact Basin: Chlorine Residual Alarm requires immediate assessment/priority grabs. Storm Intake Mode increases sampling until raw/settled stability. Sample Backwash Recovery Tank after consequential returns. Clearwell Level Controller coordinates storage/production. Distribution Dispatcher receives production-limit/demand-risk notices; North Distribution Pressure Station/South Distribution Pressure Station influence pumping. Chemical Supplier Driver delivers verified chemicals; Residuals Hauler removes residuals.

SCADA Historian Server (Lantern) retains synchronized operating records, accepted laboratory timestamps with associated trend intervals for repeatable audit reconciliation.

New part:
S101: Planned maintenance is controlled through a work order process that ties each task to an approved operating window, a named responsible person, and a defined return-to-service condition.
S102: The Chief Operator reviews the next-day schedule with operations staff so that treatment capacity, water quality risk, and distribution demand are understood before work is released.
S103: The Maintenance Planner is also known as Quarry for internal radio coordination during maintenance planning discussions.
S104: The Maintenance Planner verifies that each work order identifies affected equipment, required isolations, parts staging, and the evidence needed to close the work.
S105: The Maintenance Planner uses the snapshot to compare planned rake work against recent mechanical loading before releasing the task package.
S106: The Duty Engineer checks proposed work against current operating constraints and may defer nonessential activity when treatment margin is limited.
S107: Lockout planning identifies electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, chemical, and stored-energy hazards before personnel enter or service plant equipment.
S108: Field isolation is verified locally by the assigned craft worker and then acknowledged by operations before the equipment is opened, adjusted, or tested.
S109: Ironwood shall remain unavailable for routine maintenance release until isolation points are tagged, verified locally, and acknowledged in the shift turnover record.
S110: Work in the North Filter Gallery and South Filter Gallery is scheduled to keep enough filtration capacity available for expected demand and wash cycles.
S111: Any planned change affecting the Clearwell Level Controller requires coordination with the High Service Pump Header operating plan before the change is applied.
S112: The Chemical Supplier Driver sends the Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log before unloading any replacement cylinders at the plant.
S113: Supplier access is limited to approved routes, assigned unloading areas, and times when an operator is available to observe chemical connections and vehicle movement.
S114: Deliveries for the Coagulant Dosing Skid are staged so that hoses, containment, and emergency washdown equipment are inspected before transfer begins.
S115: Chemical work near the Chlorine Contact Basin is coordinated with operating staff so that ventilation, gas monitoring, and communications are available during the task.
S116: Shift communication includes the status of open isolations, temporary operating limits, unavailable equipment, and any abnormal condition that could affect the next crew.
S117: The Distribution Dispatcher is informed before maintenance changes the availability of the High Service Pump Header, North Distribution Pressure Station, or South Distribution Pressure Station.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
